title: Add support for local Snowflake OAuth authentication
description:
This commit implements [the new `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_CODE` authenticator][0], which is a standard OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE targeting desktop applications.

It serves as a drop-in replacement for `externalbrowser` auth, and has the benefit of working even without SSO. Plus it's easier to configure.

Under the hood it uses Snowflake's built-in `LOCAL_APPLICATION` integration, which requires no custom security integration setup.

Finally, it's also hooked into the existing keyring subsystem, and given that refresh tokens last 90 days by default, this is likely to mean *dramatically* fewer browser logins than the existing browser flow (which requires it every four hours).

Closes #41.

[0]: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-local-applications

title: fix: has_expired reports true if token is expiring within 5m
description: The comment indicates that we should consider tokens expired within 5 minutes of their expires_at, but the code was checking for 5 seconds.

title: Add support for the 'host' field in connections.toml files
description:
This commit threads through the new `host` field supported by other Snowflake SDKs. When present it takes precendence over the `account` field when constructing the Snowflake URL.

In my understanding it's mainly used for private endpoints on SPCS or privatelink accounts.

Unit tests are included.

title: Add initial support for workload identity authentication
description:
This commit introduces the first part of supporting Snowflake's new "workload identity" authenticator. Specifically, it adds support for workload identity using [the generic `OIDC` provider][0], which targets Kubernetes -- though we're also planning to support it on Posit Connect.

Pretty comprehensive unit tests are included.

[0]: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/workload-identity-federation#authenticate-to-snowflake-using-a-custom-openid-connect-oidc-provider

title: Improve error reporting when the login flow fails
description: Previously you'd get a pretty cryptic error; with these changes we get actual error codes and message back from Snowflake.

title: Add support for "connection caching" in the system keyring
description:
This commit adds support for what Snowflake calls "on-disk connection caching", which really boils down to storing a separate token in the system keyring so that `externalbrowser` authentication only requires the user to open a browser once every few hours instead of once per session.

Caching makes a nice quality of life improvement if you have to restart your R session or run something that uses Snowflake credentials (like an `rsconnect` deployment) in a separate process.

I've attempted to use the same keyring format that the Python Connector uses so that Windows and macOS users can share tokens between R and Python -- Snowflake don't themselves support using the keyring on Linux, but we do.

Unit tests are included.

I can confirm that this works for me in desktop RStudio on Linux but wouldn't mind a spot check that it works on other operating systems, too.

title: Add a table of supported auth methods to the README
description: This should help clarify what we do and do not support and allows us to clean up the Limitations, too.

title: Improve error messages when connections.toml is missing a default
description:
Previously when `connections.toml` existed but lacked the requested connection (or a "default" section), the error message erroneously claimed the file was "missing or empty".

This commit makes the error messages more specific: they now clearly state which connection is missing and provide helpful suggestions including the option to use a different connection by name.

Fixes #26.

title: Improve error messages when connections.toml does not exist
description:
Previously when a named connection was requested but the `connections.toml` file did not exist, the error message suggested defining a section in the non-existent file without acknowledging it was missing. This commit adds a more useful error message in this case.

Additionally, error messages for default connections now correctly refer to the `[default]` section instead of an empty `[]` section.

Fixes #23.

title: Fix misleading warnings when both configuration files exist
description:
Previously we warned if we detected if both files were present, but this is perfectly valid configuration in many cases. This commit instead focused on warning when both files define connections, which is *not* valid configuration.

Fixes #25.

title: Add support for 'externalbrowser' authentication
description:
This commit adds the machinery to support the "externalbrowser" authenticator, which is an interactive sign-in flow for users with access to a local browser. It includes session caching, which is a nice ergonomic improvement for repeated calls.

(The underlying protocol is completely bespoke to Snowflake so it took me a little while to get it actually working.)

You can test it as follows:

    snowflake_connection(
      account = <account>
      user = <username>,
      authenticator = "externalbrowser"
    ) |> snowflake_credentials()

This should open a browser window to the account's SSO provider.

Unfortunately this is all highly interactive code, so there is not much to unit test.
